text:
Jordan (Sales): Hey team - client finished POC evaluation today. Request to fully sweep POC assets by EOD Friday. Need confirmation on keys, pools, and any retained data.
Alex Chen: Thanks. Do they want a soft handoff (retention for 30d) or full purge now?
Jordan (Sales): They signed the termination clause — want keys revoked and data removed. Legal asked to preserve audit logs for 90d though.
Maya Kapoor: Got it. We'll rotate/invalidate keys, but keep logs for 90d in the compliance bucket. Need list of key IDs + which pools were used.
Samir Patel: Pools used: dedicated-poc-01 (4xA100), burst-poc-spot-03. Also hosted API keys: poc-hosted-abc123, poc-hosted-def456.
Jordan (Sales): Adding here the contact at client: @rachael.hunt (security). She confirmed purge.
Alex Chen: Plan: 1) Revoke Hosted API keys 2) Drain and mark Dedicated pools as decomm 3) Wipe KV/prefix caches for POC models 4) Snapshot audit logs -> compliance bucket 5) Delete snapshots after 90d.
Maya Kapoor: Approve. Two notes: - Make sure server-side request logs are redacted for PII before copying. - We need a KMS export record for the rotation event.
Samir Patel: I'll run the pool teardown today in canary, then full. Teardown commands:
```bash
# revoke hosted keys
redwoodctl keys revoke --key poc-hosted-abc123
redwoodctl keys revoke --key poc-hosted-def456

# drain dedicated pool
redwoodctl pools drain --pool dedicated-poc-01 --timeout 1800
# delete pool (after drain)
redwoodctl pools delete --pool dedicated-poc-01 --force
```
Jordan (Sales): @Alex can you confirm we also remove cached KV from the model runner? Client worried about persisted prompts.
Alex Chen: Yes. KV purge command below, will run after revokes:
```bash
redwoodctl kv purge --scope poc-terahealth --confirm
```
Samir Patel: For burst-poc-spot-03 I'll remove capacity to avoid accidental invoices, then delete the pool in 2h if no errors.
Maya Kapoor: Security checklist: - Keys revoked (screenshot) - Pool delete audit events captured - KMS rotation entry - Redaction proof for logs - Legal confirmed 90d audit retention. Please attach artifacts to the ticket.
Jordan (Sales): I'll create the post-POC ticket and add artifacts. Tagging @rachael.hunt for visibility.
deploy-bot: Deployment pipeline: job `poc-cleanup/teardown` started by Samir. Build #2047 -> running.
infra-oncall: Quick heads-up — when you delete pools, please ensure fallback routing is disabled to avoid spill traffic to other customers.
Samir Patel: Acknowledged. I'll disable routing rules first: `redwoodctl routes update --disable poc-routing-rule`
Alex Chen: After all done, I'll run a smoke test against hosted endpoints to confirm 401 on old keys and that no model inference works.
Jordan (Sales): Timeline: revokes + routing disable (now), pool drain (in 1h), deletion + kv purge (in 2h), audit snapshot -> compliance bucket (immediately). If all good, I'll send closure email to client and legal.
Maya Kapoor: Sounds good. If any unexpected data surfaces, pause deletion and ping Security.
Jordan (Sales): Thanks everyone. Please post short artifact links once done. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: Will post links to the ticket. Starting step 1 now.
deploy-bot: job `poc-cleanup/teardown` completed successfully in 6m.
Samir Patel: Pools drained and deleted, hosted keys revoked. KV purge queued, KMS rotation logged. Links: https://redwood.internal/tickets/POC-4523/artifacts
Alex Chen: Ran smoke test — old keys return 401, no inference reachable. Attached logs.
Maya Kapoor: Compliance snapshot uploaded, logs redacted and stored at s3://redwood-compliance/poc-4523/90d/
Jordan (Sales): Closing the loop with client + legal now. Thanks team!
Jordan (Sales): NOTE: keeping ticket open until 90d retention window expires (audit-only).
